question: Can the 40-byte LoadAsset_Blocking Asset parm be built as an allocator-free POD FSoftObjectPtr, skipping MakeSoftObjectPath entirely?
verdict: DIRECT PATH NOT VIABLE - required FNames are not interned in the live process

layout_gate.method: genuine UE 5.4.4 headers + MSVC 14.38 compile-time sizeof (template-instantiation extraction); CoreUObject headers compile standalone with the Core define set
member_order_source: TPersistentObjectPtr (UObject/PersistentObjectPtr.h): exactly two members, declared order: mutable FWeakObjectPtr WeakPtr; TObjectID ObjectID; (no TagAtLastTest in 5.4)
layout_gate.offsets_derivation: member sizes sum EXACTLY to sizeof at every level (8+32=40, 16+16=32, 8+8=16), so there is no padding and offsets are forced prefix sums - arithmetic, not a guessed offset
layout_gate.allocation_free_construction: YES in principle - an all-zero SubPathString is a valid empty FString (no buffer), and our target path has no ':' subobject delimiter, so the whole 40-byte parm would be POD given two FName values. Destruction is also allocator-free because we own the buffer and never invoke a destructor on it.

fname_gate.method: read-only enumeration of the live FNamePool (35 blocks, 138250 entries) using ERI's verified addressing; strings compared exactly
fname_gate.positive_control: MirrorTableRow FOUND at entry_id 0x72e0 - proves the enumerator resolves real names, so a miss is a genuine absence and not a broken scan
fname_gate.consequence: The two FName values needed for a POD FSoftObjectPtr do not exist in the running process. Creating them means interning new names, which is an engine call (FName construction from a string), i.e. exactly the allocator/runtime dependency this variant was meant to avoid. Mounting a container and registering its IoContainerHeader therefore does NOT intern the package/asset FNames - a concrete, useful negative finding.

decision: STOP direct path. Proceed to variant 1: derive FMemory::Realloc and FMemory::Free with independent provenance each (no guessed vtable slots), then use the reflected MakeSoftObjectPath -> LoadAsset_Blocking path.
